catalog_policy: These are metadata records, not imported transcriptions. Dates are approximate institutional descriptions, not exact calendar dates. No text is represented as a DSS reading until a manuscript passage, fragment/column, transcription edition, and reading are individually verified. Digital images remain at the rights holder's site; no image files are bundled.

records.name: Temple Scroll (11Q19)
records.date_estimate: Not assigned in this initial record; consult the manuscript edition and current institutional catalogue
records.date_basis: No date copied into this record without a directly verified dating statement
records.contents: A long legal-religious composition concerning the Temple and related laws; the Israel Museum identifies it as the longest Dead Sea Scroll and describes it as rewriting material from Deuteronomy
records.condition: Surviving manuscript; exact fragment and column coverage must be checked in the digital catalogue
records.holding_institution: Israel Museum, Shrine of the Book
records.image_access: Use the institutional viewer. Check current reproduction rights before copying images.
records.caution: Do not treat this composition as a manuscript copy of Deuteronomy. It is a distinct composition that reworks legal material. Exact coverage and readings require column-level verification.

records.name: Great Psalms Scroll (11QPsᵃ / 11Q5)
records.contents: A Psalms scroll that also preserves a hymn passage cross-referenced with Sirach 51:13–20 and the first two words of Sirach 51:30.
records.image_access: Consult the Qumran-Digital transcription and the IAA Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library. Image reproduction rights must be checked with the holding institution.
records.status: metadata catalogued; nine Sirach-related Hebrew transcription lines imported as a separate passage layer
records.caution: 11Q5 is a Psalms scroll, not a dedicated Sirach manuscript. Preserve the scroll's identity and layout; cross-link only the Sirach hymn passage. QDR's parallel-reference labels and display-line numbers are editorial aids, not manuscript text or physical line coordinates.

records.name: Genesis Apocryphon (1QapGen)
records.date_estimate: Approximately 25 BCE–50 CE in the cited Israel Museum educational publication
records.contents: An Aramaic retelling or expansion of portions of Genesis; the cited publication describes surviving material as a reworking of part of Genesis
records.condition: Fragmentary; not a complete copy of Genesis
records.holding_institution: Israel Museum, Shrine of the Book
records.image_access: Use the institutional digital viewer; reproduction rights must be checked with the holding institution.
records.caution: The standard Qumran identifier is 1Q20; the descriptive abbreviation 1QapGen is also used. This is an Aramaic retelling/expansion of Genesis, not a direct copy of the book of Genesis.

records.name: Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ)
records.date_estimate: Approximately 120–100 BCE in the cited Israel Museum educational publication
records.date_basis: Institutional publication's approximate dating; not an exact date
records.contents: A substantially complete copy of Isaiah; the Israel Museum describes it as the only biblical scroll preserved in its entirety
records.condition: Exceptionally well preserved relative to most DSS manuscripts
records.holding_institution: Israel Museum, Shrine of the Book
records.image_access: View images through the Israel Museum Digital Dead Sea Scrolls or the IAA Leon Levy Digital Library. Do not copy images into this app without permission.
records.caution: This is a manuscript witness to Isaiah, not a source for every wording in a modern edition. Any comparison must identify the exact column and line and distinguish preserved letters from reconstruction.

records.name: War Scroll (1QM)
records.date_estimate: Not assigned in this initial record; consult the manuscript edition and current institutional catalogue
records.date_basis: No date copied into this record without a directly verified dating statement
records.contents: A sectarian war composition also known by the descriptive title War of the Sons of Light Against the Sons of Darkness; listed by the Israel Museum among the original seven scrolls discovered in 1947
records.condition: Surviving scroll; exact column and fragment condition should be checked in the institutional viewer
records.holding_institution: Israel Museum, Shrine of the Book
records.image_access: Use the institutional viewer. Check current reproduction rights before copying images.
records.caution: This is a sectarian composition, not a book of the Hebrew Scriptures. Do not confuse its title with a historical account of a specific war without evaluating the text.

records.name: Pesher Habakkuk / Commentary on Habakkuk (1QpHab)
records.date_estimate: Approximately 50 BCE in the cited Israel Museum educational publication
records.contents: A commentary on the first two chapters of Habakkuk; the Israel Museum publication describes it as the only known copy of this commentary
records.condition: Relatively complete scroll compared with many fragmentary DSS witnesses
records.holding_institution: Israel Museum, Shrine of the Book
records.image_access: Use the institutional digital viewer; reproduction rights must be checked with the holding institution.
records.caution: This is an ancient interpretive commentary, not a manuscript copy of the full book of Habakkuk.

records.name: Community Rule (1QS)
records.date_estimate: Approximately 100–75 BCE in the cited Israel Museum educational publication
records.contents: A community rule text; the cited publication describes it as the most complete copy of the Community Rule
records.holding_institution: Israel Museum, Shrine of the Book
records.image_access: Use the institutional digital viewer; reproduction rights must be checked with the holding institution.
records.caution: This is a community rule document, not a copy of one of the Hebrew Scripture books.

catalog_limitations: This initial register is selective, not a complete catalogue of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

The IAA uses imaging-plate fragment numbers that may differ from the published manuscript and fragment numbering used in the Discoveries in the Judaean Desert series; do not treat them as interchangeable without a verified concordance.
A manuscript title or book name does not prove that every chapter or verse survives in that witness.
No Dead Sea Scrolls transcription is bundled by this metadata file.
